recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up FHIR-core work is needed for FHIR-16735 unless a later CDS work-group decision changes PlanDefinition action definition semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-16735 was a Published/Persuasive CDS STU3 ballot request for the clinical reasoning module's simple referral creation action. It objected to a nested <reference value="#referralToMentalHealthCare"/> because PlanDefinition action definition references are canonicals, not Reference elements.
initial_application: Jira records the issue as applied in git-svn commit f91f58dcb6becb9517319f3e607fa460623f2253, which changed the build-scope clinical reasoning fragment from nested Reference syntax to a canonical definition value. The earlier bac90582b2346bd2e75178f244ebdeb9080d1f60 commit had already made the same conversion in the authoritative PlanDefinition example.
additional_context: The clinical reasoning topic is in current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml, and PlanDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issue FHIR-18186 made PlanDefinition.action.definition[x] a canonical-or-uri choice, and commit 72f0fdf2f469beee28bee541c8c5e0280fc8883c updated authoritative examples to definitionCanonical. The already-published FHIR-16762 AutoFHIR commit updated copied clinical reasoning inline fragments to definitionCanonical as well, and current reference/datatype prose allows canonical fragment identifiers.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current cited clinical reasoning fragments and authoritative PlanDefinition example already use <definitionCanonical value="#referralToMentalHealthCare"/>, so no source edit was necessary.
